```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
library(fmristore)
library(fmridataset)
set.seed(1)
```

`fmristore` writes `fmridataset::fmri_frame` objects to HDF5 and opens them
again without reading the arrays. A frame is a set of observation x feature
matrices (assays) with typed observations, features, entities and tables;
`fmridataset` defines it, `fmristore` stores it.

## A frame to store

Here the observations are 8 time points from two runs, and the features are
three parcels of a small masked volume. `parcel_space()` records which voxels
belong to each parcel, so the parcellation travels with the data.

```{r frame}
dims <- c(4L, 4L, 2L)
voxels <- volume_space(dims, support = 6:27, template = "toy")
cluster <- rep(c(3L, 7L, 10L), length.out = 22)
parcels <- parcel_space(
  voxels,
  parcel_ids = c(3L, 7L, 10L),
  membership = Matrix::sparseMatrix(
    i = seq_along(cluster), j = match(cluster, c(3L, 7L, 10L)), x = 1, dims = c(22L, 3L)
  ),
  atlas = "toy-atlas"
)

n_time <- c(run1 = 5L, run2 = 3L)
observations <- axis_frame(data.frame(
  .obs_id = paste0("t", 1:8),
  run_id = rep(names(n_time), n_time)
))
signal <- matrix(rnorm(8 * 3), nrow = 8, ncol = 3)

frame <- fmri_frame(
  assays = list(signal = signal),
  observations = observations,
  features = feature_axis(data.frame(.feature_id = feature_ids(parcels)), space = parcels),
  active_assay = "signal"
)
```

## Write and reopen

`write_frame_h5()` streams each assay into a temporary file beside the
destination and renames it into place only after everything is written, so a
crash never leaves a half-written file under the final name.
`open_frame_h5()` reads the manifests; the arrays stay on disk.

```{r write-open}
path <- tempfile(fileext = ".h5")
write_frame_h5(frame, path)
frame_store_info(path)$status

reopened <- open_frame_h5(path)
class(assay(reopened, "signal")$source)
```

Selections read only what they need:

```{r read}
run2 <- filter_observations(reopened, run_id == "run2")
collect_assay(run2, "signal")

# Parcel structure survives the round trip
Matrix::colSums(parcel_membership(space(reopened)))
```

Writing to an existing path requires `overwrite = TRUE`, and a failed
overwrite leaves the previous file untouched.

```{r overwrite}
tryCatch(write_frame_h5(frame, path), error = function(e) conditionMessage(e))
```

## Appending runs: sharded stores

A sharded store is a directory of immutable frame files plus a manifest.
Each append writes a new shard, so earlier data is never rewritten.

```{r shards}
store <- tempfile("store")
run1 <- filter_observations(frame, run_id == "run1")
run2 <- filter_observations(frame, run_id == "run2")

write_sharded_frame_h5(run1, store, shard_id = "run1")
append_frame_shard_h5(run2, store, shard_id = "run2")
frame_shard_manifest(store)[, c(".shard_id", ".n_observation")]

combined <- open_sharded_frame_h5(store)
nrow(collect_assay(combined, "signal"))
```

If a writer is interrupted, `recover_frame_store()` reports, and with
`action = "rollback"` removes, the temporary files it left behind:

```{r recovery}
recover_frame_store(store)
```

## Reading HDF5 arrays directly

`h5_array_source()` describes one two-dimensional HDF5 dataset as a lazy
`fmridataset` source. It holds no open file handle, so it can be serialized
and reopened elsewhere. `h5_read_plan()` estimates how many stored values a
selection touches before reading anything.

```{r array-source}
array_file <- tempfile(fileext = ".h5")
h5 <- hdf5r::H5File$new(array_file, mode = "w")
h5$create_dataset("values", robj = matrix(as.double(1:600), 20, 30), chunk_dims = c(10L, 10L))
h5$close_all()

src <- h5_array_source(array_file, "/values")
source_shape(src)
source_read(src, observations = c(2L, 1L), features = 1:3)

plan <- h5_read_plan(src, observations = 1:5, features = 1:5)
plan$amplification # stored values touched per value requested
```

The 5 x 5 corner lies in one 10 x 10 chunk, so reading it touches 100 stored
values for 25 requested: an amplification of 4. `validate_h5_read_amplification()`
turns such an estimate into a check that fails above a chosen limit.

```{r cleanup, include = FALSE}
unlink(c(path, array_file))
unlink(store, recursive = TRUE)
```

## Legacy classes

`H5ParcellatedMultiScan`, `H5ParcellatedScan`, `H5ParcellatedScanSummary` and
`LabeledVolumeSet` remain for packages that have not yet moved to frames.
They are frozen and will be removed; new code should store frames.
`migrate_parcellated_h5()` and `migrate_labeled_h5()` convert existing files
to frames.
